objective: Computation. On splices whose near side is the Fano plane or census 58, drop the handle's homology parities by taking the union of the knot's solutions over the four homology sectors of a torus embedding (sign twists along non-contractible cycles, which keep every face condition). Does creation at the opened cut disappear, for which embeddings, and does dropping one parity suffice? Control: unions with single point flips.
status: Proved by PLANAR-COMPOSE-20261102-001B-P001 (finite classification): cutting a handle open (uniting the near solutions over the four homology sectors of a torus embedding) removes all creation for some embeddings and cut positions and not for others; the outcome depends on where the cut curves run, even within one homology class; dropping one parity cuts the Fano splices' 240 new knots to 9-23, and point-flip unions (control) never remove creation; so homology carries most of the creation, but 'a handle creates exactly what its homology parities add' fails as stated in point values
title: Cutting a handle open
